narrative.summary: Georgia has no AI law or stand-alone AI strategy. AI is governed through the 2023 Law on Personal Data Protection, which regulates decisions based solely on automated processing and requires impact assessments, and a binding 2020 National Bank regulation on risk management of AI and machine-learning models used by banks and other lenders. The Digital Governance Strategy 2025-2030 calls for an ethical and legal framework for AI in the public sector, and in February and March 2026 the Government and the Ministry of Economy gave the ministry's technology department a mandate to promote AI development.
lead_institutions: Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development

instruments.current_status: In force. Adopted 14 June 2023 and published on matsne.gov.ge on 3 July 2023 (registration code 010100000.05.001.020936); most articles, including art. 19 on automated decisions, apply from 1 March 2024 and art. 31 (data protection impact assessment) from 1 June 2024 (art. 90). It replaced the Law on Personal Data Protection of 28 December 2011 (art. 89). Amended several times, most recently by Law No. 1694-Vმს-XIმპ of 10 June 2026 (published 15 June 2026); consolidated versions on matsne.
instruments.summary: Georgia's general data protection law, enforced by the Personal Data Protection Service. Art. 19 gives data subjects the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling, that has legal or similarly significant effects, unless based on explicit consent, necessary for a contract or authorised by law, and art. 13 gives a right to information about automated decisions and the logic involved. Art. 31 makes a data protection impact assessment mandatory where processing using new technologies is likely to create a high risk, including when fully automated decisions with legal, financial or similarly significant effects are taken.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Main binding rules in Georgian law on automated decision-making and profiling by AI systems.

instruments.summary: Binding National Bank of Georgia regulation that sets a risk-management framework for data-driven statistical, AI and machine-learning models used by commercial banks, non-bank depository institutions, microfinance organisations and lending entities. It requires model-risk policies and procedures covering development, implementation, testing, internal validation and accuracy thresholds, a three-lines-of-defence split of responsibilities, and validation requirements for purchased models; certain 'supervisory models' need NBG risk assessment and consent before use.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Georgia's only AI-specific binding regulation found; governs AI/ML credit and risk models in the financial sector.

instruments.current_status: Approved by Government of Georgia Resolution No. 100 of 3 April 2025, published on matsne.gov.ge on 7 April 2025 and effective on publication. The strategy text is attachment 1 of the resolution page. Georgia has no stand-alone national AI strategy; this is the government strategy with an AI component.
instruments.summary: The Government's digital governance strategy for 2025-2030, coordinated with the Digital Governance Agency. It notes that Georgia has no single definition, legal framework or central inventory of AI systems used by public institutions, and states that the state needs a unified vision and strategy for introducing AI and other emerging technologies in the public sector. It recommends reviewing AI opportunities for digital services and accessibility and pre-emptively developing an ethical and legal framework for AI regulation based on international standards.
